messages.content: a child tried to read a sentence and could not finish it. i want to say something kind without saying it is easy when it is hard for them.
you could say: that part is hard right now. we can take it one piece at a time.
can i ask which word they want help with?
yes. that gives them a way to show the part they need, rather than having you choose it for them.
write the two parts together.
that part is hard right now. which word would you like help with?
what if they want me to read the whole sentence first?
you can do that if it helps, then let them try again. hearing the whole sentence may give context for the part that is hard.
make that a request from the child.
could you read the whole sentence first? then i would like to try it myself.
should i say they will get it right on the next try?
not for sure. you can give help and time without knowing how the next try will go.
make that explanation shorter.
you can help them try again without saying for sure that the next try will be right.
only give the first kind sentence.
that part is hard right now.
what is the difference between i worked when she called and i was working when she called?
i was working when she called clearly puts the call during your work. i worked when she called is less clear about when the work started and may need more context.
show a clear example with was working.
i was working at my desk when my sister called.
does that say i started work because she called?
no. it puts you in the middle of working at the time of the call.
what if her call made me start the work?
you could say: after my sister called, i started working.
now make it clear that the call stopped the work for a while.
i was working when my sister called, so i stopped to talk with her for a while.
can you know i finished the work later?
not from that sentence. it gives the part when you stopped for the call, not whether you finished later.
what else would you need to know?
i would need to know whether you returned to the work and finished it after the call.
now add that i did finish after the call.
i was working when my sister called, so i stopped to talk. after the call, i returned to my work and finished it.
write a story about a person with little time at the market. they should choose the things needed for one meal instead of trying to do everything.

a woman came to the market with only a short time before going home. she had a long list for the week, but knew she could not find everything before leaving. she looked at what she needed for dinner that day: rice, vegetables, and eggs. she bought those first. when she had a few minutes left, she chose one other thing from the list, then went home. she had not finished every part of the week plan, but she had what she needed for the meal. at home, she kept the rest of the list for another day rather than saying the whole task had gone wrong.
what helped her choose what to buy first?
she used the goal of making dinner that day. the things for that meal came before the rest of the week list.
did buying less mean she forgot the other things?
no. she kept them on the list for another day.
what information would you need to know whether she could buy more?
i would need to know how much time was left, how far the other things were, and when she needed to leave.
why not just tell her to stay until the whole list is done?
because she had to leave. a useful plan needs to work with the time she has, not give her work she cannot finish before leaving.
say that in fewer words.
because she had to leave. the plan should work with the time she had.
finish with dinner ready, without saying how the whole week went.
she put the list away and cooked the meal with what she had bought. the family sat down to eat that evening.
my friend said yes to a walk, then said they need to stay home. i am sad, but i do not want to make them explain everything.
you can give both parts in a kind way: i wanted to walk with you, but i understand you need to stay home. you do not have to explain everything.
can you make that less long?
i wanted to walk with you, but you do not have to explain why you need to stay home.
can that sound like i do not care why?
you can make the choice clear: i can listen if you want to talk, but you do not have to explain.
only give that message without the explanation.
you can say: i can listen if you want to talk, but you do not have to explain.
now put that with saying i wanted the walk.
i wanted to walk with you. i can listen if you want to talk, but you do not have to explain why you need to stay home.
should i say i am not sad if that is not true?
no. you can say you are sad about the change without saying your friend must change their answer.
make that a short message.
i am sad we cannot walk today, but i understand you need to stay home.
only give the part about listening.
i can listen if you want to talk.
three people want to read and two want to draw. one person wants both. how many different people have a choice on that list?
four different people, if the one who wants both is in each group. two want only reading, one wants only drawing, and one wants both.
why not five?
the person who wants both is in each group. if you add three and two, you give that same person a place in each group, even though they are one person.
show why four is enough for the real people.
two want only reading, one wants only drawing, and one wants both. those are four different people.
now explain why just adding how many are in each group gives more.
the person who wants both is part of the three and also part of the two. adding three and two gives that person a place again.
now the person who wants both chooses only drawing. how many want reading?
two people want reading now.
how many want drawing?
two people still want drawing: the person who already wanted only drawing and the person who changed their choice.
are there fewer different people now?
no. there are still four different people. changing a choice does not take a person out of the whole group.
make that answer shorter.
no. the same four people are still in the group.
the shop is open until five. does that mean it opens at five?
no. it says the shop is open up to five. it does not give the opening time.
what important detail do you still need?
we still need to know when it opens.
what if i say the shop opens after five?
then it will start being open later than five. that is different from being open until five.
can you know how long it is open from either sentence alone?
no. open until five does not give the starting time, and opens after five does not give the closing time.
what would you need for the whole open time?
no. to know the whole open time, you need when it starts and when it finishes.
now i say it opens at two and closes at five.
then it is open for three hours.
if i go there at four, should it be open?
from the hours you gave, four is during the open time. if those hours are still correct, the shop should be open then.
only give the answer about how many hours it is open.
three hours.
write a story about someone going to another room and then not knowing what they wanted to ask. make a note useful for the question rather than the answer.

a man was reading a page when he found a sentence he did not understand. he went to ask his sister about it, but on the way he stopped to answer the phone. after the call, he remembered that he had wanted help, but not which sentence it was. he returned to the book and found the place again. this time, he wrote the sentence on a small page and took it with him. when he came to his sister, the note kept the question clear. he still needed her explanation, but he did not need to keep the whole sentence in his mind while walking through the house.
what did he forget after the phone call?
he forgot which sentence he wanted to ask about.
did the note already have the answer?
no. it had the sentence he needed help with.
why was it still useful?
it let him look at the sentence when he needed to ask, instead of having to remember every word.
make that explanation shorter.
he could look at the note instead of keeping every word in his mind.
what could he say when he comes to his sister?
could you help me understand this sentence? i wrote it down so i could show you the right one.
make that a little shorter.
could you help me understand the sentence on this page?
finish with him returning to the book after the answer.
he said thank you, took the note back to the table, and read the sentence again with the new explanation in mind.
someone asked whether i can cook. i know how to make a few simple meals, but i am still learning. help me answer.
i can make a few simple meals, and i am still learning.
can i say i cannot cook at all?
that would leave out what you can already do. if you know a few meals, saying that gives a better picture than saying you can do nothing.
say that in fewer words.
saying you can make a few meals gives the real detail. it does not say you know everything, and it does not say you know nothing.
what if they ask me to cook something i have never made?
you can say you have not made it before and need to learn. you do not have to give a sure yes just because you can cook other meals.
write that reply.
i have not made that before. i would need to learn how before saying i can cook it well.
can you make it less long?
i have not made that before, so i would need to learn first.
now only give my first answer again.
i can make a few simple meals, and i am still learning.
does still learning mean i have learned nothing?
no. it says you are learning more. you can know some things already and still have more to learn.
